- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.7), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility or rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, consider mean reversion: if price is above 20-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.3), model often overfits recent trends; apply a “smooth filter” — average last 5–7 days’ true values before forecasting.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, model often fails to adjust; check for “sentiment reversal lag” — if sentiment drops below 0.2 after 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 3–5 days.
